# Thin-gauge aluminium products: literature reference

<!-- Generated by `python -m physicroll.band_products --write docs/thin-gauge-products.md`; do not edit by hand. -->

## What this is and is not

This is a literature survey of thin-gauge aluminium products: gauges, alloys, tempers, properties, rolling routes, quality requirements and named band or streak defects. Every value is quoted from four research reports (battery and electronics foil, a second battery report on alloy and temper by gauge, packaging and household foil, heat-exchanger stock, litho and other strip) and carries its source ids. It is not a validation: nothing here was measured on a plant, vendor and trade pages are low-confidence, and several standards were read from previews only. A value inside a published span is not evidence that a pass is good.

Per-pass reductions are computed by `physicroll.band_products` from the published gauge sequences as 1 − h_exit/h_entry (per sheet for a doubled pass); a block of n passes shows its total and the equal-split mean 1 − (h_exit/h_entry)^(1/n). Ranges are kept as ranges, and the reports' disagreements and "not found" lists are kept below.

Source ids: `BF-` battery report, `BG-` second battery report (alloy and temper by gauge), `PK-` packaging report, `HX-` heat-exchanger and litho report. A citation such as [PK-S20] shows the sources; a fact whose own read status is weaker than its sources shows it, e.g. [PK-S14; vendor_or_trade_page]. Read-status legend:

| Read status | Meaning | Report tags mapped onto it |
|---|---|---|
| full_text | page or document read in full (or the relevant pages) | FT; F |
| excerpt | long excerpts, previews or partial reads | EX; F with "excerpt", "preview", "partial" or "clauses"; every F of the heat-exchanger report ("full text or long excerpt") |
| abstract_or_snippet | abstract or search snippet only | S; A; no tag (non-vendor) |
| vendor_or_trade_page | vendor, producer or trade page (low confidence) | VP; V; V/A; no tag (vendor); BF-S17 (tagged FT, a trade page) |
| memory_unverified | researcher's memory, unverified | MEM; M |
| computed | computed by this module from published gauges | report "calc." values are recomputed |

Catalogue: 27 products, 1081 sourced facts, 163 sources. Status: LITERATURE_SURVEY_UNVALIDATED.

### Battery schedules: most important flag

Most important flag of the battery report: the two schedules quoted in earlier versions of this project's documentation as single-sheet battery-foil practice (260→135→65→30 µm and 280→120→55→24 µm) come from the trade page BF-S17. There the next pass is listed as 24×2→12×2 µm and 28×2→15×2 µm, i.e. doubled. So 30 µm and 24 µm are doubling-entry gauges for one-side-bright foil, not single-sheet final gauges. The trade page's first-plant row prints "302→152", which the report reads as 30×2→15×2 µm. [BF-S17]

"Tension lines": longitudinal stripes at 5–20 mm pitch appear below 15 µm and worsen as gauge falls; drivers are tension, roll roughness, roll parallelism, roll pressure and pass reduction. [BF-S21]

## General foil-rolling reference

### Per pass reduction

- Per-pass reduction "about 50 %", with five passes to 18–20 µm. [PK-S1]
- About 50 % per pass in an industrial 1200 trial from 0.4 mm. [PK-S27]
- 44.0–60.0 % [computed from PK-S2, PK-S3, PK-S16]: Span of the published packaging foil passes (PK-S2 household and converter, PK-S3 TRC 8079, PK-S16 Yennora); the report prints 46–54 % for PK-S2 and 44–60 % for PK-S3.
- Battery foil: three to six foil passes, 29–64 % per pass; BF-S12 calls 5–6 passes from ≤0.24 mm stock the industry norm. [BF-S12]

### Closed gap

- Closed gap: roll contact begins at 0.1–0.2 mm [PK-S1]; "<100 µm" [PK-S2]; "~0.080 mm" [PK-S4]. [PK-S1, PK-S2, PK-S4]
- Roll force is ineffective for gauge below about 50 µm. Tension is the fine control and speed the coarse control (the "speed effect", through oil-film hydrodynamics). [PK-S1, PK-S4]
- An Achenbach mill uses position control at 300 µm and constant force on the doubled final pass. [PK-S28]

### Doubling threshold

- Doubling starts below 20 µm and is necessary below 10–15 µm [PK-S1]; below 25 µm [PK-S26]; below 30 µm [PK-S29]; at ≤50 µm (Impol practice) [PK-S18]. EN 546-4 lets double-rolled product run to 70 µm and single-rolled start at 35 µm. [PK-S1, PK-S26, PK-S29, PK-S18, PK-S11]
- Battery foil: pack rolling covers 5–20 µm; single rolling is feasible for 9–20 µm; the Mino finishing mill minimum is 1×12 µm or 2×6 µm. [BF-S18, BF-S25]

### Speeds

- Last pass limited to about 600 m/min for lustre. [PK-S1]
- 600–1000 m/min schedule values. [PK-S2]
- Foil-mill design maxima 2000–2250 m/min. [PK-S28]
- Battery foil-mill builder maxima 1500–2200 m/min. [BF-S24, BF-S26]
- Single-stand cold mills 1200–1500 m/min maximum; foil mills up to 2500 m/min. [HX-S37]
- Strip reaches about 100 °C per pass, with 3–4 passes and coil cooling between. [HX-S36]

### Mill types

- Mill types: roughing 0.7 → 0.012 mm, intermediate 0.12 → 0.006 mm, finishing 0.05 → <0.006 mm. [PK-S28]

### Oil and rolls

- Rolling oil: kerosene base with fatty acid, alcohol or ester additives [PK-S1]; alcohol 2–5 % and ester 1–3 % [PK-S29]. [PK-S1, PK-S29]
- Oil 20–40 °C in roughing, 40–60 °C in finishing; rougher rolls for roughing, finer for finishing. [PK-S29]
- Roll roughness about equals foil roughness after one pass. [PK-S3, PK-S27]

### Doubling and surfaces

- Roll-side faces are bright and the foil-to-foil faces matt; single-rolled foil is bright on both sides. [PK-S6, PK-S26]
- The matt face is made of slip steps across the rolling direction, and pinholes are local shear-through from deep matt-side valleys. [PK-S1]

### Separating

- Separation, trim and slitting happen in one operation at 300–600 m/min, with light-box inspection for porosity and roll holes. [PK-S1]

### Final anneal

- Final anneal (O temper): slow heating, metal at 240–280 °C, up to 70 h depending on coil width and diameter, good ventilation, controlled cooling. Aims: dry, flat (no "heat pockets"), non-sticky foil. [PK-S1]
- Dryness trades off against stickiness; double-bright foil is the most sticky-prone, and >99.5 % Al risks coarse grain. H18 lidding foil is used as-rolled, without anneal. [PK-S1]

### Foil stock

- Kerth foil stock: 0.5–0.7 mm, annealed dead-soft before foil rolling, from 5–8 mm hot band or cast strip; stock tolerance ±5 % along length and ±1 % across width, to avoid edge corrugation. [PK-S1]
- Hindalco foil stock: 0.2–0.6 mm ±5 %, tempers "M" (as-rolled, Rm 125–180 MPa), H14 or H16; flatness <20 I-units, wedge ≤0.7 %; from DC ingot and concast. [PK-S23]
- Twin-roll cast is described as limited to pure or low-alloy grades [PK-S5]; it is used industrially for 1235, 8011, 8079, 8006 and 8021 with a homogenisation step [PK-S3, PK-S31]. [PK-S5, PK-S3, PK-S31]

### Flatness

- Flatness: no numeric foil limit found; Kerth uses waviness W = 100·f/L % and notes stretching is practical only above about 100 µm. [PK-S1]

### Wettability

- Wettability: EN classes A (water), B (+10 % ethanol), C (+20 %), on to G; A–C acceptable. ASTM equivalent: dry-annealed A / B / C, or "slick". [PK-S11, PK-S12]

### Alloy roles

- Alloy roles (largely vendor statements, consistent with the EN 546-2 strength ranking): 1235 / 1145 / 1200 softest, best rollability to 6 µm; 8079 (Fe 0.7–1.3, Si 0.05–0.3) more strength and elongation at thin gauge than 1xxx; 8011 / 8011A (Al-Fe-Si) general-purpose, the hard-temper lidding alloy; 8021 / 8021B (Fe 1.2–1.7) highest O-temper elongation (≥12 % at 45 µm), hence cold forming; 8006 (Al-Fe-Mn) strongest (O-temper Rm 80–140 MPa), for containers and down-gauged household foil; 3xxx rigidity in containers. [PK-S9; vendor_or_trade_page]
- 5052 appears only for single-rolled technical foil. [PK-S18]

### Foil surface defects (EAFA catalogue)

| Defect | Appearance | Published cause | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rolling stripes | Gloss side only, constant along the rolling direction. | Local work-roll wear, or rolls damaged by foreign material from casting or foil stock. | PK-S7 |
| Heat stripes | Grey, straight to snaking. | Temperature or flatness differences across the width, or a locally overheated roll. | PK-S7 |
| Gloss difference | Matt side only. | Unstable separating-oil application at doubling. | PK-S7 |
| Broken matt | Bright spots on the matt side. | Too much deformation or too high speed in the doubled pass. | PK-S7 |
| Chatter marks | Not described beyond the name in the report. | Mill or grinder vibration. | PK-S7 |
| Grooves | Not described beyond the name in the report. | Unfavourable flatness profile. | PK-S7 |

### Standards

- EN 546-1: Covers 6–200 µm. Defines converter foil (6–200 µm, single or double rolled), consumer foil (10–24 µm) and container foil (single-rolled, 35–200 µm). [PK-S8]
- EN 546-2: Mechanical properties: 15 mm strip, 50 or 100 mm gauge length; Table 1 (O and H18 by gauge band), Table 2 (container tempers; partly garbled in the report's read). [PK-S9]
- EN 546-3: Tolerances: single spot ±6 % single-rolled, ±8 % double-rolled; lot average ±6 / 5 / 4 % (single) and ±8 / 6 / 4 % (double) for ≤3 t, 3–10 t, >10 t; width ±1 mm up to 1000 mm, ±2 mm above; weighing is the referee method. [PK-S10]
- EN 546-4: Pinholes are <0.2 mm in 6–20 µm foil; roll holes are >0.2 mm and periodic; light box 1000–1500 lux, ignore <0.02 mm; limits by agreement; burst test for consumer foil, Erichsen for container foil. [PK-S11]
- ASTM B479-19: Annealed foil, ≥98 % Al, 6.4 µm to <150 µm; alloys 1100, 1145, 1235, 8011, 8079, 8111; thickness ±10 % per roll; tensile by agreement; pinholes by B926 with no numeric limit (≥50 µm "virtually free"). [PK-S12]
- GB/T 3198-2020: Local thickness ±6 % (ordinary) or ±5 % (high precision) at ≤9 µm, ±5 % or ±4 % above; lot average ±5 / 4 / 3 %; pinhole limits per grade (third-party transcription). [PK-S14]
- GB/T 22638: Test methods: .1 thickness, .2 pinholes, .3 stickiness, .4 wetting tension, .5 wettability, .6 DC resistance, .7 heat-seal strength. [PK-S14]
- YBB00152002-2015 (China, pharma lidding): No pinholes >0.3 mm; ≤1 per m² at 0.1–0.3 mm; burst ≥98 kPa; heat seal ≥7.0 N/15 mm to PVC. [PK-S15]
- ASTM B373: Capacitor foil, 4.3–12.7 µm, 1145 / 1235. The report does not say which capacitor foil type it covers. [PK-S13]
- EN 573-3: Chemistry only; not read directly. [PK-S9]
- EN 683-1/-2/-3: Finstock: scope 60–400 µm, unclad only; 3003 and 1050A properties by temper; gauge ±6 % single reading, average ±5 / ±4 / ±3 % for lots ≤3 t / 3–10 t / >10 t; width ±0.2 to ±1.0 mm; the O/H22/H24 table was not read. [HX-S17]
- EN 485-4: Applies above 0.20 mm: ±0.02 mm for 0.2–0.4 mm at ≤1000 mm width (soft-alloy group); strip flatness is not specified. [HX-S18]
- EN 485-1 with special requirements: How litho strip is ordered, plus qualification. [HX-S19]
- ISO 12635: Litho plate thickness ±0.010 mm; CtP edge wave ≤3.0 mm (1.5 mm recommended). [HX-S35b]

## Battery foil: alloy and temper by gauge

From the second battery survey (sources `BG-`): which alloy and temper are used at each gauge. A process engineer can read off, for a final gauge: the alloys, the temper label, the standard minimum and typical strength, and the evidence. The tool uses the proposals below when the plant has not stated a material; each carries the status LITERATURE_PROPOSAL_TO_CONFIRM_WITH_PLANT and must be confirmed or corrected by the plant.

### Three findings first

1. No source gives a hard "gauge X → alloy Y" rule. What exists is a strength floor that rises as gauge falls; producers meet it by moving from 1085/1070/1060/1235 to Cu-bearing 1100-type or 1C30-type alloys. [BG-G2, BG-G6, BG-G11, BG-G21]
2. The first survey's 8011 figure was wrong: the GB/T 33143-2022 minimum for 8011 is 180 MPa, not 220–230 MPa. [BG-G2, BF-S2]
3. "H18" on battery foil is a label for a strength table. The foil gets 97–99 % cold reduction after the last anneal, far above the 75 % that defines H18, so European sources call the same product H19. [BG-G40, BG-G8, BG-G26, BG-G14, BG-G17]

How the standard minima were read: GB/T 33143-2022 Table 9 minima (all H18) were read from a producer page that reproduces the table, cross-checked against the garbled draft translation and against T/ZZB 2638-2022, which copies four of its rows. Where the table sets no value for an alloy in a band, none is given here. An official copy of Table 9 was not found. [BG-G2, BG-G1, BG-G3]

Evidence ratings are the report's own (strong / medium / weak / vendor-level), kept as data: "minima" rates the standard minima of the band, "choice" rates the usual alloy choice.

- Elongation: GB/T 33143-2022 elongation minima are 1.0–3.0 %, depending on alloy, gauge length and one- or two-side-bright; 8A21 is ≥4.0 %. [BG-G2]
- Temper label: Temper as written: H18 in GB/T 33143, T/ZZB 2638 and JIS H 4160; "H18, H19" in T/ZZB 1203, Gränges, Symetal and Armor; "H19" at Innoval. "H18" on battery foil is a label for a strength table: the foil gets 97–99 % cold reduction after the last anneal, far above the about 75 % that defines H18, so European sources call the same product H19. Both labels are consistent with collector foil. [BG-G2, BG-G3, BG-G25, BG-G4, BG-G14, BG-G15, BG-G18, BG-G17, BG-G40]
- Surface: Single-sheet two-side-bright foil is preferred. [BG-G17]
- Surface: Sam-A rolls single-sheet down to 10 µm and says Japanese mills double at 10 µm. [BG-G11]
- Surface: UACJ sells 10 µm 8021 as bright/matte (one-side-bright). [BF-S4]
- ≤10 µm: The ≤10 µm band first appeared in GB/T 33143-2022. [BG-G21]
- >15–20 µm: The report rates the cell-type column vendor-level and gives no separate rating for the alloy column; the usual-choice rating is recorded as vendor_level. [BG-G19, BG-G42]
- >20–30 µm: GB/T 33143 stops at 20 µm: no standard minima above it. [BG-G2]

### The two bands that matter for a 17–19 µm and a 12 µm product

- A usual final gauge of 17–19 µm is in the **>15–20 µm** band; 12 µm is in the **>10–13 µm** band. From 50 µm in two equal single-sheet passes (computed): 50→18 µm is 40 % per pass (50→30→18 µm), 50→12 µm is 51 % per pass (50→24.5→12 µm).

**18 µm: band >15–20 µm.** Proposals:

- standard: **1235-H18**; Rm 210 MPa used (middle of the typical range 200–220 MPa; range 175–220 MPa); Rp0.2 185 MPa (assumed: not published for 1235 in this band; assumed Rp0.2 = 0.881 x Rm, the median Rp0.2/Rm ratio of the hard-foil grades that publish both at 15 µm (span 0.862–0.924; computed)); evidence vendor_level. Rule: the usual standard-strength choice of the gauge band (first in the report's list). [BG-G2, BG-G42, BG-G19]
- high-strength: **1100-H18**; Rm 220 MPa used (the standard minimum (a lower bound); range ≥220 MPa); Rp0.2 193.8 MPa (assumed: not published for 1100 in this band; assumed Rp0.2 = 0.881 x Rm, the median Rp0.2/Rm ratio of the hard-foil grades that publish both at 15 µm (span 0.862–0.924; computed)); evidence weak. Rule: no usual choice of this grade is published for the band: the option of this grade with the highest standard minimum (ties: the report's order) is used, rated weak. [BG-G2]

**12 µm: band >10–13 µm.** Proposals:

- standard: **1235-H18**; Rm 180 MPa used (the standard minimum (a lower bound); range ≥180 MPa); Rp0.2 158.5 MPa (assumed: not published for 1235 in this band; assumed Rp0.2 = 0.881 x Rm, the median Rp0.2/Rm ratio of the hard-foil grades that publish both at 15 µm (span 0.862–0.924; computed)); evidence medium. Rule: the usual standard-strength choice of the gauge band (first in the report's list). [BG-G2, BG-G21, BG-G23]
- high-strength: **1100-H18**; Rm 250 MPa used (middle of the typical range 230–270 MPa; range 230–310 MPa); Rp0.2 220.2 MPa (assumed: not published for 1100 in this band; assumed Rp0.2 = 0.881 x Rm, the median Rp0.2/Rm ratio of the hard-foil grades that publish both at 15 µm (span 0.862–0.924; computed)); evidence medium. Rule: the usual high-strength choice of the gauge band (first in the report's list). [BG-G2, BG-G14, BG-G21, BG-G23]

The research-stated numbers for 12 µm: standard minimum 180–190 MPa for 1235/1060, 230 MPa for the 1100/1C30 type that EV practice favours [BG-G2, BG-G21, BG-G23].

### Options by band

Order: Presentation order (a rule of this module, never a claim that one alloy is best): options the research calls the usual choice at this gauge first, then by evidence rating (strong, medium, weak, vendor_level, not_rated), then by strength (middle of the first typical range, else the standard minimum) from high to low, then by name. Options outside their published gauge span or usual only for another surface come after the others.

Proposal rule: standard = the usual standard-strength choice of the gauge band (first in the report's list); high-strength = the usual high-strength choice of the gauge band (first in the report's list); when there is none, no usual choice of this grade is published for the band: the option of this grade with the highest standard minimum (ties: the report's order) is used, rated weak. Strength value used: the middle of the first published typical tensile range for this alloy in this band; if none, the standard minimum (a lower bound: finished foil is usually above it), else the lowest published typical minimum. Proof strength, where not published, is assumed from the median Rp0.2/Rm ratio of the 15 µm grades that publish both (computed).

- Pouch: Laminates: 35 µm in an 88 µm laminate; 40 µm in 113 and 153 µm laminates. [BG-G30]
- Pouch: 8021-O is confirmed for pouch foil by Symetal (35–40 µm) and Innoval (40–50 µm). [BG-G15, BG-G17]

### Why alloy and temper change with gauge

1. Constant line force: "thinning alone gives insufficient strength per unit width and foil breaks on the coating line", so strength must rise as gauge falls. One broker report puts numbers on it: 20 µm ≥170 MPa, 13 µm ≥190 MPa. [BG-G6, BG-G22]
2. The floor keeps rising: 1070 minimum 150 MPa (GB 2016) → 160 (2019 group standard) → 185 (GB 2022); 1100 170 → 180 → 230 (read from a flattened chart). The ≤10 µm band first appeared in 2022. [BG-G21]
3. Calendering: higher compaction breaks strip, so buyers raise strength and elongation together; ≥200 MPa is common, some ask ≥270; a conventional route gives 200–230 MPa at 3.4–3.9 %. [BG-G21]
4. Conductivity against strength: 3003 costs 11–13 points of IACS, so producers strengthen 1xxx instead. In 2009: 1085 for automotive high-power cells; 1N30 general; 1100, 3003, 8021 for consumer lines run at high productivity. [BG-G6, BG-G7]
5. Observed shift: Sam-A's A1100 (10–17 µm) rose from 4.6 % of sales in 2012 to 73 % in 2020 as demand moved from ≥15 µm to ≤12 µm. [BG-G11]
6. Strength after drying: drying softens hard foil, purer foil most; one patent requires ≥230 MPa as rolled and ≥210 MPa after drying. [BG-G7, BG-G26]
7. Rollability and stability: 2xxx, 5xxx, 6xxx and 7xxx are "extremely difficult to roll to foil"; 1xxx, 3003 and 8021 all passivate in LiPF6. Cu above 0.2 % caused foil-rolling breaks. [BG-G41, BG-G26]
8. Sodium-ion: aluminium on both electrodes, 800–900 t/GWh against 350–400 (NMC) and 450–550 (LFP); 12–15 µm conventional, 8–10 µm thin. [BG-G21, BG-G39]

### How each temper is produced

| Temper | Definition | How battery foil reaches it |
|---|---|---|
| H18 | Strength of about 75 % cold reduction after a full anneal. [BG-G40] | Last anneal at 0.5–2.5 mm, or none after hot rolling; none in the foil mill. Computed: 0.5 mm → 15 µm is 97 % (strain 3.5); 1 mm → 12 µm is 98.8 % (strain 4.4). [BG-G8, BG-G26, BF-S8, BF-S18] |
| H19 | Minimum Rm at least 10 MPa (2 ksi) above H18. [BG-G40] | Same route, more strain or solute. T/ZZB 1203 puts H19 20 MPa above H18. [BG-G4] |
| High-strength grades | Sold as H18 or H19. [BG-G26, BG-G8] | Cu 0.05–0.2 % (1100, 1C30); Fe and Mn held in solution by hot homogenising and no intermediate anneal; starting cold rolling at ≥1 mm so strain reaches 4–5 instead of about 3, which raised strength and elongation together. [BG-G26, BG-G8] |
| H2x | Strain hardened, then partially annealed. [BG-G40] | Not used in any public collector-foil specification. [BG-G40] |
| O | Fully annealed. [BG-G40] | Pouch foil: rolled hard, then coil-annealed at 240–260 °C for 40–45 h; the anneal also removes rolling oil. [BF-S32, BF-S33, BG-G44] |

### Correction

- 8011 GB/T 33143-2022 minimum corrected: 180 MPa [BG-G2], not the "about ≥220–230 MPa" high-strength group the first survey read from the garbled draft translation [BF-S2]. The first-survey entry is kept for 1C30 and 1100 only; 8011 now carries 180 MPa. [BG-G2, BF-S2]

### Disagreements (second survey)

- 8011 minimum: 180 MPa [BG-G2] against 220–230 MPa in the first survey [BF-S2]. [BG-G2, BF-S2]
- H18 or H19: Asian standards say H18; European producers say H18/H19 or H19 for the same product. [BG-G2, BG-G3, BG-G25, BG-G4, BG-G14, BG-G15, BG-G17, BG-G18]
- Group standard below national: T/ZZB 1203-2019 (160–200 MPa) is lower than GB/T 33143-2022 (175–230 MPa), even in its H19 column. [BG-G4, BG-G2]
- 1060 strength: GB minimum 185–190 MPa; Gränges 180–230 MPa; a trade article claims 230–250 MPa. [BG-G2, BG-G14, BG-G20]
- "Mainstream" alloy: 1060 and 1235 in Chinese sources; 1100 at Sam-A; 1085, 1N30, 3003 in Japan. [BG-G20, BG-G22, BG-G11, BG-G7]
- Gauge by cell type: vendor pages put 1070 at 10–12 µm for consumer cells and 1060 at 15–20 µm for storage, with no data. [BG-G19]
- Soft collector foil: some reseller pages list O temper; no standard or producer datasheet supports it, and the second survey treats it as an error. [BF-S48, BG-G2]
- Cu in 1100: one trade article warns of micro-galvanic corrosion; no measurement was found. [BG-G20]

### Not found (second survey)

- GB/T 22648-2023 Tables 5–9 (pouch-foil strength, cupping, pinholes by gauge); every mirror drops them. T/ZZB 2076-2021 is known only from a reseller summary. [BG-G28, BG-G29]
- An official copy of GB/T 33143-2022 Table 9; the draft translation's host was outside the research session's allowed network domains for direct download.
- Any cell-maker purchase specification, and any LFP-against-NMC rule for gauge or alloy.
- Datasheets with numbers from Lotte, Dong-IL, Dongwon, Novelis, Hydro, Constellium, Hindalco, Assan, Dingsheng, Nanshan, Wanshun, Yong Jie, Xiashun, Shenhuo; Speira's page gives gauge only (12–20 µm). [BG-G16]
- JIS H 4160:2006 itself; the mirror carries the 1994 text. [BG-G25]
- Recrystallisation temperature by alloy for hard foil: Furukawa-Sky plots it but the values are not extractable; one vendor page says 1235-H18 softens fast above 220 °C. [BG-G7, BG-G43]
- Any standard for thick collector foil or tab foil.

## 1. Li-ion cathode current-collector foil (`battery_collector_foil`)

Family: battery_electronics. Rolled: single or doubled. Two-side-bright (bright/bright) foil is rolled single-sheet to final gauge; the report's single-sheet schedules are two-side-bright. Doubled (pack) rolling gives one-side-bright foil: UACJ sells 10 µm 8021 as bright/matte and the BF-S17 schedules finish with a doubled pass. Single rolling to final gauge is feasible for 9–20 µm; below 9 µm high-strength foil is "difficult" single, and pack rolling covers 5–20 µm. The Mino battery finishing mill minimum is 1×12 µm or 2×6 µm. [BF-S4, BF-S11, BF-S12, BF-S13, BF-S14, BF-S15, BF-S16, BF-S17, BF-S18, BF-S25]

### Gauge

- Final gauge: 8–20 µm [BF-S1]. GB/T 33143-2022 scope; width ≤1600 mm; bare and coated.
- UACJ offers 12, 15 and 20 µm bright/bright and 10 µm 8021 bright/matte. [BF-S4]
- Sam-A 12–20 µm; Dongwon 10, 12, 13.5, 15 and 20 µm. [BF-S45, BF-S46]
- 9–10 µm is mature, 8 µm double-bright is in mass production, 7 µm is possible. [BF-S21]
- Single-sheet final gauge: 9–20 µm [BF-S18]

- Roughing work-roll Ra 0.15–0.28 µm. [BF-S11, BF-S12, BF-S13, BF-S16]

- Work-roll diameter 200–320 mm (catalogue) and 280 mm (one mill listing). [BF-S27]
- Rolling oil: base oil 80#/82# (viscosity about 1.75) or 95# (2.05) with 3–11 % ester and alcohol additives; oil temperature 38–45 °C, or 50–65 °C in BF-S12. More additive lowers dyne. [BF-S12, BF-S13, BF-S16]
- Foil Ra 0.07–0.22 µm both sides, side-to-side difference ≤0.03 µm, residual carbon <5 mg/m². [BF-S9]
- Measured Ra 0.094 µm on 13 µm 1070-H18. [BF-S51]

### Quality requirements

- Thickness tolerance: GB/T 33143: ±5 % ordinary, ±4 % high, ±3 % ultra-high precision. [BF-S2]
- Thickness tolerance: A patent targets ±3 %. [BF-S12]
- Thickness tolerance: Some customers now ask ±2 %. [BF-S21]
- Flatness: GB/T 33143 wave height at 8 N/mm²: ≤5 / 3 / 2 mm at 1.0 m roll span and ≤10 / 8 / 4 mm at 1.5–2 m (ordinary / high / ultra-high precision). [BF-S1]
- Flatness: Customer practice: sag ≤5–8 mm at 2 m. [BF-S12]
- Flatness: Customer practice: ≤5 mm across width. [BF-S21]
- Wettability: GB/T 33143: ≥30 mN/m, recommended. [BF-S1]
- Wettability: Customers ≥32 mN/m. [BF-S12]
- Wettability: Mino mill design ≥33 mN/m. [BF-S25]
- Wettability: Speira corona-treated ≥34 mN/m. [BF-S10]
- Wettability: Corona treatment at the slitter adds 1–3 dyn. [BF-S12]
- Pinholes: GB/T 33143 maximum per m² at ≤10 µm: 15 (ultra-high) / 20 (high) / 30 (ordinary). [BF-S2]
- Pinholes: GB/T 33143 maximum per m² at 10–13 µm: 6 / 10 / 15. [BF-S2]
- Pinholes: GB/T 33143 maximum per m² at 13–15 µm: 3 / 5 / 10. [BF-S2]
- Pinholes: GB/T 33143 maximum per m² at 15–20 µm: 0 / 3 / ordinary grade not captured in the report's read. [BF-S2]
- Other: GB/T 33143: burr ≤150 / 100 / 50 µm, no splices, on-line pinhole and surface annexes. [BF-S1, BF-S2]
- Other: Carbon-coated foil: GB/T 33143 coating areal-density class 0.30–2.00 g/m². [BF-S1]
- Other: Carbon-coated foil vendors: 0.6–2 µm per side on 12–16 µm base, dyne ≥40–64. [BF-S49]

| Tension lines | Longitudinal stripes at 5–20 mm pitch; appear below 15 µm and worsen as gauge falls. | Drivers: tension, roll roughness, roll parallelism, roll pressure and pass reduction. | BF-S21 |

### Standards

- GB/T 33143-2022: Battery foil: 8–20 µm, width ≤1600 mm, bare and coated; alloys and H18; tolerance classes; flatness; wettability; pinholes; burr; no splices; streak defects forbidden when severe. [BF-S1, BF-S2]
- EN 546-2: No battery table; H18 minima 135 MPa (1050A), 140 MPa (1200), 160 MPa (8011A). [BF-S31]
- DIN 50154 and EN 546-2: Speira tests to these. [BF-S8]

### Caveats

- Most important flag of the battery report: the two schedules quoted in earlier versions of this project's documentation as single-sheet battery-foil practice (260→135→65→30 µm and 280→120→55→24 µm) come from the trade page BF-S17. There the next pass is listed as 24×2→12×2 µm and 28×2→15×2 µm, i.e. doubled. So 30 µm and 24 µm are doubling-entry gauges for one-side-bright foil, not single-sheet final gauges. The trade page's first-plant row prints "302→152", which the report reads as 30×2→15×2 µm. [BF-S17]
- The GB/T 33143 property table was partly garbled in the report's read; the minima are quoted as "about". [BF-S2]
- 8011 GB/T 33143-2022 minimum corrected: 180 MPa [BG-G2], not the "about ≥220–230 MPa" high-strength group the first survey read from the garbled draft translation [BF-S2]. The first-survey entry is kept for 1C30 and 1100 only; 8011 now carries 180 MPa. [BG-G2, BF-S2]

Key requirement: Thickness ±3–5 % by precision class, wave height ≤2–5 mm at 1.0 m span, wettability ≥30 mN/m, pinhole limits by gauge (GB/T 33143). [BF-S1, BF-S2]

Evidence: Gauge-by-gauge alloy and temper: see the battery grade table (minima strong; usual choice medium to strong by band, vendor-level at >15–20 µm, weak above 20 µm). [BG-G2, BG-G21, BG-G19, BG-G35]

Alloy and temper by gauge: see "Battery foil: alloy and temper by gauge" above.

- EN 546-1: Covers 6–200 µm. Defines converter foil (6–200 µm, single or double rolled), consumer foil (10–24 µm) and container foil (single-rolled, 35–200 µm). [PK-S8]

### Rolling route and schedules

- Final cold-work windows: 20–40 % [HX-S3], or 20–35 % at 45–80 µm with interanneal at 275–400 °C [HX-S5]; an H14-type temper is set by a final reduction of roughly 20–40 % after the interanneal. [HX-S3, HX-S5]
- TRC route: cast 6–8 mm → 0.1–0.6 mm → interanneal 350–450 °C for 1–4 h → final reduction ≥45 % (60–90 % preferred) to 50–70 µm. [HX-S4]
- Mitsubishi: interanneal 460–600 °C for under 4 h, final reduction 15–50 %. [HX-S6]
- Interanneal temperature matters: 500 °C instead of 350 °C gave finer post-braze grain and worse sag (32 mm against 24 mm). [HX-S3]
- Clad fin under 80 µm loses brazeability because filler diffuses into the core. [HX-S16]
- Pre-braze strength must fall as gauge falls, for corrugation forming. [HX-S8]
- 3003 work hardening after a 420 °C/2 h anneal: +23 MPa UTS going from 15 to 25 % reduction, and +31 MPa from 25 to 35 %. [HX-S40]

**HX-S3 DC route 3.5–4 mm → 0.080 mm** [HX-S3]. Multi-pass to about 1 mm, then to 0.123 mm, interanneal 350 °C × 4 h at 50 °C/h, then 35 % final reduction; pass counts not given.

Key requirement: Coated 5182-H48: UTS ≥365 MPa, YS 331–362 MPa; ±5 µm; edge wave ≤3.2 mm. [HX-S38]

- Battery cell case: 3003 or 1050, O or H14, 0.30–0.80 mm [BF-S42]; prismatic can wall 0.7–1.5 mm [BF-S43]; GB/T 33824-2025 governs [BF-S44]. [BF-S42, BF-S43, BF-S44]
- Insulation facing / tape: 8–70 µm double-rolled, 50–100 µm single; 1200, 1050A, 8006, 8079; O / H18; both modes. [PK-S18]
- Child-resistant lidding: Al 9–25 µm in paper/PET/Al/HSL, or 20–25 µm Al + 15–20 µm PVC; 8011; soft or hard; doubled; total laminate 80–135 µm; peel-push = paper/PET/Al/HSC. [PK-S21, PK-S20]
- Sachet / pouch laminate: 6–7 and 8–12 µm (7 / 9 / 12 µm); 8079, 1235, 8011; O; doubled; as converter foil. [PK-S21, PK-S22]
- Chewing-gum / confectionery: 6–7 µm + paper 20–35 g/m²; alloy not found; O; doubled; fold retention, embossing. [PK-S25]
- Butter wrap: 6.5–7 µm + paper; 8011, 1235; O; doubled; one vendor only. [PK-S33]

## Disagreements between sources

### General

- Gauge at which doubling starts: <20 µm and necessary below 10–15 µm [PK-S1]; <25 µm [PK-S26]; <30 µm [PK-S29]; ≤50 µm (Impol practice) [PK-S18]. EN 546-4 lets double-rolled product run to 70 µm and single-rolled start at 35 µm. [PK-S1, PK-S26, PK-S29, PK-S18, PK-S11]
- Closed-gap onset: 100–200 µm [PK-S1], <100 µm [PK-S2], about 80 µm [PK-S4]. [PK-S1, PK-S2, PK-S4]
- Thickness tolerance: EN ±8 % and ASTM ±10 % versus vendor claims of ±3–5 %. [PK-S10, PK-S12]
- Wine-capsule foil gauge: 6–10 µm versus 16–50 µm. [PK-S33]

### Li-ion cathode current-collector foil

- 1xxx strength: EN 546-2 H18 minima are 135–140 MPa, Speira standard ≥165 MPa, GB/T 175–190 MPa, UACJ typical 180–185 MPa. One vendor page claims 1060 at 230–250 MPa and 1100 above 270 MPa, which fits only the high-strength variants. [BF-S31, BF-S9, BF-S2, BF-S3, BF-S4, BF-S48]
- Passes and reductions: three to six foil passes; 29–64 % per pass. BF-S12 says the industry norm is 5–6 passes from ≤0.24 mm stock. [BF-S11, BF-S12, BF-S13, BF-S14, BF-S15, BF-S16]
- Final single-sheet speed: 450 m/min (thermal-softening argument) versus 1000–1200 m/min claimed. [BF-S11, BF-S12]
- Minimum single-rolled gauge: about 9 µm, 12 µm on the Mino mill, UACJ sells 10 µm as bright/matte, yet 8 µm double-bright is reported in production. [BF-S18, BF-S25, BF-S4, BF-S21]
- Rolling mode in BF-S13: the text says "doubled rolling" on the finishing mill while calling the product two-side-bright. [BF-S13]
- Temper: H18 is the consensus; some vendor pages list O. [BF-S1, BF-S48]
- BF-S17 doubled passes: the report lists them as 24×2→12×2 µm and 28×2→15×2 µm, yet reads the trade page's first-plant row "302→152" as 30×2→15×2 µm; which schedule the 28×2→15×2 µm pass belongs to is not stated. Both readings are carried. [BF-S17]

### Battery pouch-laminate barrier foil

- Toyo minima (75–85 MPa, 9–10 %) sit well below Chinese typical values; GB/T 22648 defaults to one-side-bright. [BF-S28, BF-S32, BF-S33, BF-S29]

### Electrolytic capacitor anode foil, low voltage

- GB/T 3615 low-voltage anode gauge: 0.015–0.080 mm in one summary, 0.050–0.150 mm in another. [BF-S36]

### Pharma blister lidding foil (push-through)

- Blister lidding alloy: 8011-H18 (Asian vendors) versus 1200 / 8079-H18 (Impol). [PK-S20, PK-S18]

### Pharma strip-pack foil

- Strip-foil burst strength: two converters quote different minimums for the same gauge. [PK-S20, PK-S22]

### Converter / flexible-packaging foil

- Pinholes at 6 µm: <500–600 per m² in vendor specs versus up to 1500 per m² in the GB ordinary grade. [PK-S32, PK-S14]
- Twin-roll cast suitability for 6–7 µm: "restricted" versus routine but pinhole-prone. [PK-S5, PK-S3, PK-S31]

### Brazed automotive fin stock (radiator, condenser, evaporator, heater, CAC)

- Final reduction for fin: 20–40 % (DC) vs 15–50 % vs ≥45–90 % (TRC). [HX-S3, HX-S6, HX-S4]
- Interanneal temperature for fin: 200–400 °C vs 350–450 °C vs 460–600 °C. [HX-S5, HX-S4, HX-S6]
- Post-braze 3003: Rm 110 / Rp 40 MPa [HX-S1] vs 122 / 67 MPa [HX-S10]. Sag tests use different overhangs (50 or 80 mm), so the values are not comparable. [HX-S1, HX-S10]
- Fin gauge floor: EN 683 stops at 60 µm, while 40–50 µm is sold. [HX-S17, HX-S4, HX-S7]

### HVAC fin stock (mechanically assembled)

- HVAC fin tolerance: ±3 % vs ±5 % (vendors) vs ±6 % single reading (EN 683-3). [HX-S20, HX-S17]

### Lithographic sheet

- Litho pass limit: ≤50 % traditional vs 57–60 % (Hydro). Interanneal gauge ranges from 0.9 to 2.4 mm, or is omitted. [HX-S25, HX-S26, HX-S27]
- Litho thickness tolerance: ±5–7 µm vs ±10 µm. [HX-S36b, HX-S35b]

## What was not found

### General

- Suppository-foil gauge and alloy.
- Numeric flatness (I-unit) limits for finished foil.
- Datasheets with numbers from Novelis, Speira, Hydro, Constellium, Carcano, Lotte or UACJ (packaging report); gauge datasheets from Novelis, Speira, Constellium, Arconic or Kobelco (the Gränges catalogue gives properties but no gauges). [HX-S1]
- Separating-oil composition.
- Work-roll roughness by pass from a primary source in stated SI units (packaging).
- A reliable wine-capsule foil specification.
- Cable shield foil: no solid numbers found.
- Cross-width thickness-profile (crown) specifications for strip.
- patents.google.com was blocked for the fetch tool in the heat-exchanger research session; those patents were read through the Exa tools.
- EN 573-3, ASTM B209, JIS H4000/H4160, GB/T 3880 and YS/T 95.1 limits were not read (catalogue records only); anything beyond their scope would be from memory. [HX-S17]

### Li-ion cathode current-collector foil

- Clean copies of GB/T 33143 Tables 4 and 9.
- Any YS/T standard for battery foil.
- EN 546-3 tolerance values and JIS H 4160 content.
- JIS H 4160 lists 1N30, 1085, 1100, 3003, 8021 and 8079 in O and H18 (the researcher's memory only, unverified). [memory_unverified]
- Work-roll diameters from Achenbach, SMS or Primetals for battery mills.
- A peer-reviewed foil-mill schedule; BF-S52, despite its title, describes a hot mill. [BF-S52]
- Datasheets with numbers from Lotte, Novelis, Hydro, Dingsheng or Nanshan.
- chinesestandard.net and ttbz.org.cn were outside the research session's allowed network domains; the standards were read through mirrors instead.

### Battery pouch-laminate barrier foil

- Clean copies of GB/T 22648 Tables 5–9.
- One secondary summary gives 8A21 ≥85 MPa / ≥16 % and pinholes ≤30 or ≤20 per m²; it is self-disclaimed. [BF-S30]
- A pass schedule for 40 µm pouch foil.
- Group standard T/ZZB 2076-2021 was not read; the second survey found only a reseller summary (≥70–85 MPa, cupping ≥5.5–7.0 mm). [BG-G29]

### Thick battery collector foil

- Any standard for thick collector foil.

### Battery tab foil and strip

- Any standard for tab foil.

### Pharma blister lidding foil (push-through)

- Hard-temper lidding rolling schedules, or pass schedules for 20–60 µm pharma gauges.

### Household foil, heavy-duty

- US heavy-duty household gauge from a producer.
- EN 546-4 burst and stickiness acceptance values.

### Brazed automotive fin stock (radiator, condenser, evaporator, heater, CAC)

- Pass-by-pass schedules for brazed fin.
- Clad-ratio tolerances.

### Brazing sheet (tube, header, plate)

- A pass schedule for brazing sheet.
- Clad-ratio tolerances.

### Lithographic sheet

- Primary-source I-unit specifications for litho or fin stock; "<2 I-units" for litho appears only on a trade blog that is not in the source list.
- Mill speeds specific to fin or litho mills.
